title: Device Authorization Flow (RFC 8628) - polling, lifecycle, provider compatibility
description: Byte-equivalent behaviour for the RFC 8628 device-authorization client across Python / TypeScript / Rust. NO HTTP MOCKING IS REQUIRED: the state machine is pure over an injected monotonic clock and a scripted response sequence, so a harness feeds `token_responses` in order and records the sleeps. Case kinds: `poll` drives the polling state machine (`poll_delays[i]` is the sleep BEFORE `token_responses[i]`; `polls_made` counts responses actually consumed); `expiry` checks TokenSet.is_expired; `refresh` checks rotation and terminal failure; `discovery_url` is pure URL construction with no network; `discovery` scripts well-known responses; `parse` checks body parsing and field-name normalisation; `request` checks body encoding and client-authentication placement; `redaction` asserts secrets never reach a debug string; `alias_validation` checks construction-time rejection; `hook` asserts the extension-hook contracts. A case carrying `repeat_last_response: true` repeats its final scripted response indefinitely. Wall-clock `now` is pinned to 1000 wherever a case asserts `expires_at`. Tracking issue: aiperceivable/apcore-toolkit#17.

test_cases.description: Token returned on the first poll.
authorization_pending continues polling and leaves the interval untouched.
An absent `interval` in the device response falls back to 5.
slow_down adds exactly 5 seconds (RFC 8628 §3.5), never a multiplier.
test_cases.notes: The canonical case from the spec. Exponential backoff would give 5,5,10,20 and trip a rate limiter written against the RFC.

test_cases.description: Two slow_down responses add 5 twice, reaching 15 - not 5*2*2.
access_denied terminates immediately; no further poll is made.
test_cases.notes: A third response is scripted deliberately. Consuming it would prove the client kept polling past a terminal state.

test_cases.description: expired_token terminates.
The client stops at expires_in even when the server never says expired_token.
test_cases.notes: Elapsed reaches 15 >= 12 on the third sleep, so the third poll never happens. Relying on the server's error alone leaves a client polling forever.

test_cases.description: The first poll happens AFTER one interval, not immediately.
test_cases.notes: poll_delays[0] == 5 rather than 0 is the whole assertion. An eager first poll races the user, who has not yet visited the verification URI.

test_cases.description: A transport failure is retried rather than terminating, still bounded by the deadline.
An unrecognised error identifier terminates as a protocol error.
A 2xx whose body carries no access_token terminates cleanly, not with a crash.
A lowercase token_type is normalised to Bearer casing.
A space-delimited scope string is split into a list (RFC 6749).
expires_at is wall-clock now + expires_in, an absolute instant.
test_cases.notes: Harness pins wall_clock_now to 1000. A duration would be meaningless after a process restart, which is why the stored form is absolute.

test_cases.description: is_expired is true inside the 30-second default skew window.
test_cases.notes: 975 + 30 = 1005 >= 1000. The token is still technically valid; the skew stops a request being dispatched with a credential that expires in flight.

test_cases.description: A token with no expires_at never auto-expires.
Outside the skew window the token is not expired - the converse of 016.
test_cases.notes: Without this, an implementation returning True unconditionally passes 016.

test_cases.description: A refreshed TokenSet REPLACES the stored record wholesale, including the refresh token.
test_cases.notes: scope becomes [] because the response omits it. Merging the new access token into the old record would keep r1 - spent and invalid under rotation.

test_cases.description: invalid_grant on refresh is terminal: clear the store, do not retry.
repr / toString / Debug must contain neither the access token nor the refresh token.
test_cases.notes: Redaction is a security property, and a property nobody tests is a property that regresses. Asserted as conformance rather than left to convention.

test_cases.description: A vendor error code mapped via error_aliases dispatches as its standard equivalent.
A form-urlencoded token response parses; the client must not assume JSON.
test_cases.notes: Some providers return form-encoded unless the request asks otherwise. The client sends Accept: application/json AND falls back to form parsing.

test_cases.description: A device response without expires_in falls back to a 15-minute deadline.
test_cases.notes: 900 / 5 = 180 sleeps to reach the deadline, so 179 polls happen. poll_delays is omitted here (180 identical entries); assert its length is 180 and every entry 5.

test_cases.description: A non-default scope_separator is used when encoding the device request.
An alias mapping onto a non-RFC identifier is rejected at construction.
test_cases.notes: Aliases may only map ONTO the four standard identifiers. Allowing new targets would let configuration introduce states the state machine has no branch for.

test_cases.description: The converse of 025: mapping onto a standard identifier is accepted.
RFC 8414 INSERTS the suffix between host and path for a path-bearing issuer.
test_cases.notes: Pure URL construction, no network. The insertion-vs-append difference is invisible until a tenant- or realm-scoped issuer appears, which is what multi-tenant providers use.

test_cases.description: OIDC Discovery 1.0 APPENDS to the issuer - candidate 3, same issuer as 026.
For an issuer with no path the two constructions collapse to the same shape.
test_cases.notes: Candidates 2 and 3 are identical here. That is expected and is precisely why the bug hides until case 026's shape shows up.

test_cases.description: An explicitly configured endpoint is never replaced by a discovered one.
grant_types_supported matching neither form warns; the flow still proceeds.
test_cases.notes: Capability detection warns rather than refuses. A provider under-reporting its grants is more common than one that genuinely cannot do device flow.

test_cases.description: authorization_pending at HTTP 428 continues polling - dispatch is on the body.
test_cases.notes: A real provider does this. A status-code-driven client treats 428 as fatal and breaks against it entirely.

test_cases.description: slow_down at HTTP 403 backs off rather than terminating.
access_denied at HTTP 403 terminates as a denial, not as a protocol error.
An interval inside the slow_down body is authoritative and overrides the +5 default.
test_cases.notes: 30, not 10. The server's own number beats guessing, and costs one conditional.

test_cases.description: verification_url is read as the verification address when verification_uri is absent.
test_cases.notes: A parser bound to the exact RFC spelling reads null here and shows the user a blank URL - a silent failure at the one step the user must act on.

test_cases.description: An error reported in `error_code` rather than `error` dispatches correctly.
Proprietary extra fields parse without error - never reject on unknown keys.
user_code reaches the consumer byte-for-byte: no upper-casing, stripping, or re-grouping.
test_cases.notes: Lowercase with a hyphen. Some providers are case-sensitive and at least one embeds the code unmodified into a URL query parameter. Presentation is the consumer's business, and even there it must stay enterable as given.

test_cases.description: authorization_declined aliased to access_denied terminates as a denial.
Without an explicit alias, invalid_grant is a protocol error - NOT silent expiry.
test_cases.notes: The over-correction guard. Normalisation makes the client permissive; this asserts permissiveness stops short of masking a malformed or already-redeemed code as benign expiry.

test_cases.description: grant_types_supported: ["device_code"] is accepted as supported.
test_cases.notes: The full URN is urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code; a provider advertising the short form still supports it.

test_cases.description: An absent grant_types_supported is treated as supported, not unsupported.
Params and headers returned by transform_request reach the outbound request.
parse_response returning None uses the built-in parser rather than failing.
classify_error returning a value outside the four identifiers is rejected LOUDLY.
test_cases.notes: The body carries a NON-STANDARD identifier on purpose. Without it a harness invents one, and an invented standard identifier resolves before the hook is reached - so the hook never runs and the case passes without asserting anything. Never coerced, never defaulted, never passed through to dispatch.

test_cases.description: classify_error returning None falls through to default classification.
test_cases.notes: Previously used `access_denied`, which resolves through normal classification and therefore never consults the hook - the case passed whatever the hook did. An unresolved identifier plus a hook returning None must fall through to the default outcome, which is a protocol error.

test_cases.description: Fixed order: error_aliases, then classify_error, then dispatch.
test_cases.notes: The alias wins because it resolves to a standard identifier before the hook is consulted. If the hook ran first the outcome would be expired_token, and the two are not interchangeable - one is the user refusing, the other a timeout.

test_cases.description: With no hooks installed, output is identical to the corresponding hook-free case.
client_secret_basic produces a Basic header on BOTH the device and token requests.
test_cases.notes: Both endpoints is the easy half to miss. A provider can reject an unauthenticated /device/authorize with invalid_client, long before any token request happens. Y2lkOnNlYw== is base64 of 'cid:sec'.

test_cases.description: The default `none` sends client_id only, with no secret anywhere.
An error body matching no known envelope yields a protocol error CARRYING the raw body.
test_cases.notes: Fail soft on shape. One surveyed provider returns some errors in the OAuth envelope and others, on the same endpoint, in a proprietary one. Crashing on a missing key loses the only diagnostic the operator has.

test_cases.description: request_encoding['refresh'] = 'json' sends JSON while the token request stays form.
test_cases.notes: One vendor's single token endpoint takes form for the code exchange and JSON for refresh. Per-kind, not a global 'uses JSON' flag, or that combination is inexpressible.

test_cases.description: A 200 serving HTML at a well-known path is NOT accepted; the next candidate is tried.
test_cases.notes: A real provider serves an SPA at one well-known path. Advancing on status alone accepts it, fails while parsing, and never tries the remaining candidates.

test_cases.description: Metadata whose issuer differs from the one used to build the URL is rejected.
test_cases.notes: The metadata is otherwise COMPLETE on purpose. Both cases previously omitted device_authorization_endpoint, so discover() threw whether or not the issuer check fired - and an implementation that normalises the issuer before comparing passed. Verified by mutation in the TypeScript SDK. Assert the rejection itself, not merely that discovery failed.

test_cases.description: Issuers differing only by trailing slash or case are DIFFERENT, not normalised equal.
test_cases.notes: The metadata is otherwise COMPLETE on purpose. Both cases previously omitted device_authorization_endpoint, so discover() threw whether or not the issuer check fired - and an implementation that normalises the issuer before comparing passed. Verified by mutation in the TypeScript SDK. Assert the rejection itself, not merely that discovery failed.

test_cases.description: A discovered endpoint on plain http:// is REFUSED. This is the hard half of the endpoint rule; case 057 is the soft half.

A discovered https:// endpoint on a DIFFERENT origin than the issuer is warned about and then FOLLOWED. Pins the 2026-09-08 amendment: the spec previously said such an endpoint was rejected, which contradicted case 029 and breaks real providers that host the token endpoint on a separate host.

RFC 6749 §2.3.1: the client id and secret are form-urlencoded BEFORE base64. Asserted as the round trip a server performs - base64-decode, split on the first ':', form-decode - because that is the property that matters. Raw concatenation fails it: the secret's '+' decodes to a space and the server sees a different secret.
test_cases.notes: Deliberately NOT an exact-bytes assertion. Python's quote_plus, JavaScript's URLSearchParams and encodeURIComponent, and Rust's form encoders disagree on how space, '*' and '~' are spelled - and all of those spellings decode identically, so a server cannot tell them apart. Pinning one spelling would force two SDKs to hand-roll an encoder for zero functional gain. What must not vary is that encoding happens at all. With Python's quote_plus the header reads 'Basic Y2lkOnMrcCUyQmElM0FjZQ==' - an example, not the contract.

test_cases.description: error_aliases does NOT apply on the refresh path. A consumer who opted into invalid_grant -> expired_token for the device-code path must still get the terminal store-clearing behaviour when refresh fails with invalid_grant.
test_cases.notes: Without this rule the one alias the spec explicitly describes would disable the one terminal rule that protects the store - the refresh path would see expired_token, treat it as non-terminal, and leave a spent refresh token on disk.

test_cases.description: When the device response omits expires_in, on_user_code receives the EFFECTIVE deadline (900), never null. A consumer rendering a countdown must be told when the client will actually give up; passing null forces every consumer to reimplement the 900 fallback, which is exactly the per-CLI duplication this proposal exists to remove.
test_cases.notes: Found as a live three-way divergence after the first implementations landed: Python applied the fallback at parse time and passed 900, while Rust and TypeScript both passed the raw wire value. Nothing in the corpus covered it.

test_cases.description: The converse of 060: when the server DOES send expires_in, that value is passed unchanged.
A form-encoded body must be a conforming application/x-www-form-urlencoded serialization: form-decoding it returns every parameter unchanged, including values containing a space, '+', '*' and '~'.
test_cases.notes: The three languages' default helpers produce three different byte strings here - quote_plus gives 'a+b%2Bc%2Ad~e', URLSearchParams 'a+b%2Bc*d%7Ee', encodeURIComponent 'a%20b%2Bc*d~e' - and all three decode back to the same value. The corpus therefore pins the round trip, not the bytes. This follows the repository's own ownership rule: byte-equivalence is for formats two consumers must compare, and the consumer here is a third-party OAuth server that decodes. 'plus_only' is the case that catches no-encoding-at-all: 'a+b' left raw decodes to 'a b'.

test_cases.description: When a caller-supplied timeout_seconds is SHORTER than the server's expires_in, on_user_code reports the timeout - the deadline actually in force - not the server's larger number.
test_cases.notes: The spec already says of timeout_seconds: 'when both apply, the shorter wins'. All three SDKs applied that to the DEADLINE and then reported the unclamped server value to the callback, so a consumer rendering 'expires in 600s' watched the flow die at 7. No divergence between the SDKs - they were consistently inconsistent with the contract. Reporting one number, the one the loop actually uses, is the only reading under which case 060's own justification holds.
